Evaluate a julia model's likelihood and gradient at given parameters

Source: R/ctJuliaBackend.R
ctJuliaEvaluate.Rd

Evaluates the objective that the julia backend optimises, the log likelihood with the random effects integrated out as intoverpop specifies, and its gradient, at a vector of raw (unconstrained) parameters. Useful for checking a fit, profiling by hand, or passing ctsem's likelihood to another optimiser or sampler.

Usage

ctJuliaEvaluate(
  object,
  pars = NULL,
  gradient = TRUE,
  contributions = FALSE,
  gradient_method = c("adjoint", "forward"),
  cores = getOption("mc.cores", 2L)
)

Arguments

object

A fit from ctFit(..., backend = 'julia'), or a model prepared without fitting by ctFit(..., backend = 'julia', fit = FALSE) (class ctJuliaModel).

pars

Raw (unconstrained) parameters, in the order of coef(fit). Defaults to the fit's estimate, and must be given for a prepared model.

gradient

Also return the gradient with respect to pars.

contributions

Return subject and row contribution details when available.

gradient_method

Either "adjoint" (reverse mode, the default) or "forward" (ForwardDiff). Both compute the same gradient. The cost of "adjoint" does not grow with the number of parameters, so it is faster, and more so for larger models. See optimcontrol$gradient in ctOptimControl.

cores

The most engine threads this evaluation uses. NA keeps the limit already set.

Value

A list containing the log likelihood and, when requested, the gradient and the contributions.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Needs a working julia backend, so the example is inert where Julia is
# absent -- including on CRAN, whose check machines have none.
if (isTRUE(ctJuliaStatus()$available)) {
  model <- ctModel(type = 'ct', manifestNames = 'Y1', latentNames = 'eta1',
    LAMBDA = matrix(1))
  model$pars$indvarying <- FALSE
  prepared <- ctFit(ctsemtestdat, model, backend = 'julia', fit = FALSE)
  start <- ctJuliaEvaluate(prepared, pars = rep(0, 6), cores = 1)
  str(start)
  # Julia keeps running between calls, holding what it has compiled;
  # this ends it.
  ctJuliaKill("session")
}
# }
